q: Under Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of:
options: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha only
President, Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
explanation: Art 79: Parliament = President + RS + LS. Though the President is not a member of either House, no bill becomes law without presidential assent.

q: [71st BPSC] The power to recruit the Secretarial staff of the Lok Sabha is vested in:
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
explanation: The Speaker controls the Lok Sabha Secretariat (Art 98) — recruitment of LS secretarial staff vests in the Speaker. The 71st BPSC's distractors included the PMO and UPSC — wrong channels for House staff.

q: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House because:
options: Its members are elected for life
It is never subject to dissolution — one-third of members retire every two years
explanation: RS is permanent (Art 83): no dissolution; members serve 6-year terms, with 1/3 retiring biennially. Option D confuses individual term with the House's continuity.

q: A Money Bill can be introduced only:
options: In the Lok Sabha, on the President's recommendation
In the Rajya Sabha, with the President's permission
explanation: Art 109/110/117(1): Money Bill only in the Lok Sabha, and only on the President's prior recommendation. RS cannot introduce, amend or reject it — just 14 days of recommendations.

q: Whose decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
explanation: Art 110(3): the Speaker's certification is final. Courts can examine procedural aspects (Aadhaar ruling 2018 tested but respected the certificate's scope) — the exam answer remains the Speaker.

q: A joint sitting of Parliament can be summoned for:
options: Ordinary bills and financial bills — but NOT Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills
Any bill deadlocked between the Houses
explanation: Art 108 joint sitting: ordinary + Financial Bills (I/II) only. Excluded: Money Bills (RS can't deadlock them) and Constitution Amendment Bills (both Houses must pass identically). Only 3 joint sittings ever: 1961, 1978, 2002.

q: Who presides over a joint sitting of Parliament?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
explanation: Art 108(2): the Speaker presides (Deputy Speaker next; then RS Deputy Chairman; never the VP — he's RS Chairman). Called by the President.

q: [71st BPSC] Which is correct about a Censure Motion?
options: It requires the President's approval to move
It is not different from a no-confidence motion
It is different from the no-confidence motion
It can only be moved in the Rajya Sabha
explanation: 71st BPSC answer: censure ≠ no-confidence. Censure targets a specific minister/act (or the CoM); it need not compel resignation (individual-censure), whereas no-confidence is against the whole CoM and forces resignation if passed.

q: The Rajya Sabha can authorise Parliament to legislate on a State List subject (Art 249) by:
options: Simple majority, valid for one year
Two-thirds majority of members present and voting, valid for one year (renewable)
Special majority with half the states' ratification
explanation: Art 249: RS resolution by 2/3 present & voting (national interest) → Parliament legislates on State List for 1 year (renewable). Art 312 (all-India services) uses the same 2/3. LS cannot pass these resolutions.

q: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha provided by the Constitution (post-104th Amendment) is:
explanation: After the 104th Amendment (2019, effective 2020) ended Anglo-Indian nomination, the ceiling = 530 states + 20 UTs = 550. (552 was the old ceiling with 2 nominated; 543 = current actual seats.)

q: The Public Accounts Committee of Parliament is chaired (by convention since 1967) by a member of:
explanation: PAC (22 members: 15 LS + 7 RS) chairmanship goes to an opposition member since 1967; ministers cannot be members. PAC examines CAG reports.

q: The quorum required to conduct business in either House of Parliament is:
explanation: Art 100(3): quorum = 1/10 of total membership (incl. presiding officer). The President can direct adjournment/suspension when quorum fails.

q: A no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha requires the support of at least:
explanation: Leave for a no-confidence motion needs 50 members' support (Rules of Procedure). Adjournment motions also need 50. If passed, the CoM must resign.

q: Which of the following is NOT a Money Bill matter under Article 110?
options: Appropriate receipts into the Consolidated Fund
Imposition, abolition or alteration of taxes
Regulation of state taxes in the public interest
explanation: Art 110's 7 heads include taxes, borrowing, CF/CAF custody, appropriation, receipts, incidental. Regulation of state taxes in the public interest (Art 274) is NOT an Art 110 head — the classic MCQ fine-print.

q: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
options: Does not vote in the first instance but casts a casting vote in case of a tie
Votes on every bill like other members
Can vote only on Money Bills
explanation: Art 99/100: the Speaker votes only in a tie (casting vote). The RS Chairman (VP) cannot vote at all except an original vote on RS resolutions — a subtle LS/RS contrast.

q: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is elected by:
options: The Rajya Sabha from among its members
explanation: Art 89: RS elects its Deputy Chairman from its members; presides in the Chairman's absence. Deputy Speaker (LS) likewise elected by LS (Art 93).

q: The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is recognised provided the largest opposition party has at least:
explanation: Leader and Deputy Leader of Opposition (Salary) Act 1977: recognition requires ≥1/10 of total LS seats (~54-55 currently — the statutory test is the fraction, not a fixed number).

q: Which committee examines the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General?
explanation: The PAC examines CAG audit reports (appropriation accounts + finance accounts). Estimates suggests economies; CoPU examines PSU performance.

q: Under Article 312, a new all-India service can be created by:
options: The Lok Sabha passing a resolution
The Rajya Sabha passing a resolution (2/3 present & voting) and Parliament enacting a law
explanation: Art 312: RS resolution (2/3 present & voting) declares necessity → Parliament enacts. Existing all-India services: IAS, IPS, IFoS — the IFoS was created via this route (1966).

q: The annual financial statement (Budget) is laid before Parliament under Article:
explanation: Art 112: Annual Financial Statement (Budget). Art 114 = Appropriation Bill; Art 117 = financial bill procedures; Art 110 defines Money Bills. The President causes it to be laid.

q: The anti-defection law is contained in:
explanation: 10th Schedule (52nd Amendment, 1985): disqualification on defection; Speaker/Chairman decide — subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan, 1992).

q: A bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its dissolution, but a bill originating in and passed by the LS, pending in the Rajya Sabha:
options: Does not lapse (RS is permanent), unless passed by LS before dissolution
Goes to the President for assent
explanation: A bill originating in and passed by LS, pending in RS at LS dissolution, does not lapse (RS continuity) — but a bill originating in RS, pending in LS, lapses on LS dissolution. Lapse rules are a BPSC staple.

q: The Speaker Pro Tem is:
options: A Rajya Sabha member nominated by the VP
The senior-most member of the new Lok Sabha, appointed by the President to administer oaths
explanation: The President appoints the senior-most member as Speaker Pro Tem to swear in the new LS and preside until the Speaker's election.

q: The Women's Reservation (106th) Amendment, 2023, provides:
options: 33% reservation for women in LS, state assemblies and Delhi — effective after delimitation following a census
explanation: Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Sept 2023): 1/3 reservation in LS + state assemblies + Delhi, effective after the post-census delimitation — the deferred-implementation clause is the exam point.

q: Which one of the following is a Rajya Sabha-exclusive power (not available to the Lok Sabha)?
options: Passing a resolution to create new all-India services (Art 312)
explanation: Art 312 (and 249) resolutions belong to the RS only. VP removal starts in RS but needs LS agreement — not exclusive; Money Bills & no-confidence are LS domains.
